title: The Fossil Record
seo_title: Grade 8 Fossil Record Worksheets: Rock Layers, Extinction and Homologous Structures
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms throughout the history of life on Earth under the assumption that natural laws operate today as in the past.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the fossil record (NGSS MS-LS4-1, MS-LS4-2): superposition, fossil time ranges, extinction, transitional fossils, and homologous vs. analogous structures. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Lower layers are older; fossils show change over time.
key_sub: The fossil record shows life becoming more diverse, with many groups going extinct. Shared bone patterns point to common ancestors.
body_html:
How to think about it

The fossil record shows the history of life. In undisturbed rock, lower layers are older (superposition), so fossils show which organisms lived when.

  • Patterns: life became more diverse and complex; many groups appeared and then went extinct.
  • Transitional fossils (like Archaeopteryx or walking whale ancestors) show features of older and newer groups.
  • Homologous structures (human arm, bat wing, whale flipper) have the same bones used for different jobs. They show a common ancestor. Analogous structures (bird and insect wings) do the same job but are built differently.
Example

A fern fossil is in the bottom layer, a shell in the top. Which is older?

Lower = older.

Answer: the fern

Example

Human arm and bat wing: same bones. What does this suggest?

Homologous structures.

Answer: a common ancestor

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the top layers are the oldest.
  • Thinking homologous structures must do the same job.
  • Thinking humans lived with non-bird dinosaurs.

faq.q: How do scientists know which fossils are older?
faq.a: In undisturbed rock layers, lower layers formed first, so the fossils in them are older (the law of superposition).

faq.q: What patterns does the fossil record show?
faq.a: Life has changed over time, generally becoming more diverse and complex, and many groups have appeared and then gone extinct.
Body parts in different organisms that have the same basic bones but may do different jobs, such as a human arm and a bat wing. They suggest a common ancestor.

items.q: What are homologous structures?
c: parts that do the same job but have different structures
body parts with similar bones in different organisms, inherited from a common ancestor
items.e: Same structure, different uses.

items.q: In Sofia's rock layers, how does the shark tooth compare in age with the fish?
items.e: Layer C is above layer D, so it formed later.

items.q: Did humans and non-bird dinosaurs live at the same time?
c: No. Non-bird dinosaurs died out about 66 million years before modern humans appeared.
items.e: Their ranges do not overlap.

items.q: What is a transitional fossil?
c: a fossil with features of an older group and a newer group
a fossil of a living animal
a fossil found on the surface only
items.e: For example, Archaeopteryx (dinosaur and bird features).

items.q: What is the fossil record?
c: all the fossils found and the order in which they appear in rock layers
items.e: It shows life's history.

items.q: What does it mean when a fossil group stops appearing in younger layers?
items.e: Extinction shows in the record.
